patterns.teaches: When one screen needs three services, compose once at the edge with bounded fan-out — not three round-trips from the client.
patterns.title: Gateway aggregation

patterns.teaches: One edge for every client — routing, auth, rate limits and the strangler route table live there, not in each service.
patterns.title: API gateway

patterns.teaches: Each consumer pins what it reads from a provider; the provider’s CI fails when it would break a consumer — independent deploys stay safe.
patterns.title: Contract testing

patterns.because: you chose event_backbone = nats, which is not none
patterns.teaches: The in-process bus becomes a broker: every topic a context publishes becomes a durable subject, published through the outbox.
patterns.title: Event-driven messaging

patterns.teaches: One coordinator owns the multi-service write: each step a local transaction, each failure a compensating step, the riskiest step last.
patterns.title: Saga — orchestration

patterns.teaches: Let the platform resolve names — compose service names, Kubernetes Services, Container Apps app names — and pass base URLs by environment.
patterns.title: Service discovery

patterns.teaches: Every cross-service read is a typed net/http client with a context deadline; gRPC is ported where the monolith already speaks it, not imposed.
patterns.title: Synchronous transport — REST at the edge, gRPC inside

patterns.teaches: Answer a cross-service query by calling the owners and joining in memory — try this before building a read model.
patterns.title: API composition

patterns.because: you chose orchestrator = azure-containerapps, which is not compose
patterns.teaches: Pods × pool size must fit under the database’s max_connections — set it, don’t inherit a default.
patterns.title: Connection-pool budget

patterns.teaches: An aggregate is the consistency boundary; what it records as having happened is the event other services react to.
patterns.title: Domain events and aggregates

patterns.teaches: Two versions of the code always share the schema during a rollout — add, migrate, then remove, never rename in place.
patterns.title: Expand–contract schema change

patterns.teaches: The same guarantee at the HTTP edge — a caller-supplied key makes a retried write a no-op.
patterns.title: Idempotency key

patterns.because: you chose event_backbone = nats, which is not none
patterns.teaches: At-least-once is reality — record each processed message id in the same transaction as its effect.
patterns.title: Idempotent consumer

patterns.teaches: A version column and a conditional UPDATE — the split widened every write window, and last-writer-wins now loses data.
patterns.title: Optimistic concurrency

patterns.because: you chose outbox = sql-outbox, which is not none
patterns.teaches: Decide who drains the outbox — one relay per service, leader-elected or SKIP LOCKED — and make sure every replica is allowed to run it.
patterns.title: Outbox relay topology

patterns.teaches: A saga has no isolation — other requests see its intermediate states, so design semantic locks and reversible steps.
patterns.title: Saga isolation countermeasures

patterns.because: you chose outbox = sql-outbox, which is not none
patterns.teaches: Write the row and the message in one local transaction, relay after commit — the only honest way out of the dual write.
patterns.title: Transactional outbox

patterns.teaches: Translate at every boundary — the consumer maps the provider’s contract into its own types, so one service’s model never leaks into another.
patterns.title: Anti-corruption layer

patterns.teaches: Put an interface in front of the in-process call, swap the implementation for a client behind it — the in-code half of the strangler.
patterns.title: Branch by abstraction

patterns.teaches: Each service owns its tables; nobody else reads them — the one invariant that makes independent deployment real.
patterns.title: Database per service

patterns.teaches: A service is a thing the business does and owns data for — catalog, orders, payments — never a technical layer.
patterns.title: Decompose by business capability

patterns.teaches: Extract a service only against a named force — team, scale, isolation or lifecycle; everything else stays in a bounded core.
patterns.title: Right-sizing

patterns.teaches: Put a gateway in front of the monolith and move one route group at a time; the monolith shrinks while production keeps working.
patterns.title: Strangler fig

patterns.teaches: Boundaries come from data ownership and co-writes measured in the shards; the model only refines names and edges it can be checked against.
patterns.title: How the cut is computed

patterns.teaches: Every service looks the same when you open it — cmd/, internal/, migrations/, one go.mod — so a reader learns the fleet once.
patterns.title: Go microservice conventions

patterns.teaches: One pinned stack, stated once — Go 1.26, a module per service in one go.work, slog + OpenTelemetry, NATS JetStream, distroless nonroot images.
patterns.title: The 2026 Go target architecture

patterns.teaches: One small shared startup path — config, slog, OTel, health, graceful shutdown — so every main.go is the same ten lines.
patterns.title: Microservice chassis

patterns.teaches: /healthz says the process lives; /readyz says it can serve — keep them different or the orchestrator restarts healthy pods.
patterns.title: Health checks

patterns.teaches: Traces, metrics and logs over one OTLP pipe; the trace id in every log line; the backend is a swap.
patterns.title: Observability — slog + OpenTelemetry

patterns.teaches: Configuration from the environment, secrets from the platform’s store via workload identity — never in git, never in the image.
patterns.title: Secrets and configuration

patterns.teaches: Validate the token at the gateway and again in each service; carry identity as a claim, not as an in-process context value.
patterns.title: Security — JWT at the edge and in every service

patterns.teaches: Test against real Postgres and NATS in containers, not mocks — the split moved the risk into the edges mocks hide.
patterns.title: Integration testing with real dependencies

patterns.because: you chose orchestrator = azure-containerapps, which is not compose
patterns.teaches: Scale HTTP services on CPU/RPS and consumers on queue depth — CPU is the wrong signal for a JetStream consumer.
patterns.title: Autoscaling — HPA and KEDA

patterns.teaches: Prove the timeouts, breakers and compensations work by breaking things on purpose, in a test environment first.
patterns.title: Chaos engineering

patterns.teaches: One static binary per service in a distroless nonroot image, deployed the same way everywhere — compose locally, Kubernetes/Helm or Container Apps in production.
patterns.title: Deployment — compose, Kubernetes, Azure Container Apps

patterns.teaches: Move traffic to an extracted service gradually — weighted routes and flags, with a fast way back.
patterns.title: Progressive delivery

patterns.teaches: Limit at the edge per client, and inside services on expensive endpoints — shed load before the database does.
patterns.title: Rate limiting

patterns.teaches: Every hop has a deadline, bounded retries with jitter for idempotent calls, and a breaker per upstream.
patterns.title: Resilience — timeouts, retries, breakers

patterns.teaches: Keep the ported package as the unit — one package per context inside the service, wiring in cmd/, adapters beside it; Go rewards fewer layers.
patterns.title: Flat package per context

patterns.teaches: Omissions are decisions — plugin architectures, space-based grids, serverless-per-function and a shared-library "platform" are not targets here.
patterns.title: Architecture styles this playbook does not apply
